Ag. 1024 (about Asclepius, whom Jupiter struck with a thunderbolt because he had brought Hippolytus back to life) οὐδὲ τὸν ὀρθοδαῆ τῶν φθιμένων ἀνάγειν Ζεὺς αὔτ᾽ (or αὐτ᾽) ἔπαυσεν ἐπ᾿ εὐλαβείᾳ [nor did Zeus cease from raising the seer of the dead, out of caution]. The words ἐπ᾿ εὐλαβείᾳ [out of caution] (changed by Triclinius to Ζεὺς αὔτ᾽ ἔπαυσ᾽ ἐπ᾿ ἀβλαβείᾳ γε [Zeus himself stopped, to his harm]) were noticed by Canterus to have been inserted by a glossator or interpolator filling a lacuna. For the sense requires something like what Weilius conjectured: εὐτε τὸν – Ζεὺς ἀπέπαυσε βέλει δαμέντα [when Zeus stopped him, subdued by the bolt].
